description: Execute Bean 0097 in holon-coherence: fix prompt prefill throughput reporting 0.00 tok/s, stop non-streaming requests from corrupting decode throughput with physically impossible 34k-38k tok/s values, guard throughput math against near-zero durations, and audit every telemetry metric for mathematical consistency across CumulativeMetrics, /holon/api/metrics, the web dashboard, the CLI scorecard and the offline wire-log parser
goal: Implement and verify changes across holon-coherence for Bean 0097: 1) PREFILL THROUGHPUT NEVER REPORTS ZERO (mitm_addon.py, commands/metrics.py): prefill_tps must equal prompt tokens divided by a genuine TTFT in seconds whenever prompt tokens > 0 and TTFT > 0. Audit every endpoint family (Anthropic, Gemini, OpenAI-compatible) so ttft is captured from the real request start and the real first-token/first-payload arrival, never defaulted to now (which yields ttft = 0.0 and prefill 0.00 tok/s). Guard against missing or zero request_start_time / response_headers_time / first_chunk_time by leaving the sample unmeasured instead of recording 0.0, so avg_prefill_throughput_tps, latest_prefill_tps, avg_tail_prefill_tps and latest_tail_prefill_tps stay faithful in CumulativeMetrics, /holon/api/metrics, holon-coherence metrics and _read_offline_metrics. 2) DECODE THROUGHPUT ONLY FROM GENUINE STREAMING (mitm_addon.py): stop computing output_tps as output_tokens / (total_time - ttft) for non-streaming responses, because headers and the full body arrive in the same network chunk so generation_time collapses to socket parse time (~0.001s) and yields absurd 34,000-38,000 tok/s values that poison the cumulative average. Compute decode throughput exclusively from real SSE chunk intervals (first_chunk_time to last_chunk_time), require a streaming response flag, and treat generation durations below a realistic 0.05s floor as unmeasured rather than as samples. Expose decode throughput as null/unmeasured for those requests and keep avg_decode_throughput_tps and latest_decode_throughput_tps averages over valid streaming samples only. 3) FULL METRIC CONSISTENCY AUDIT (mitm_addon.py, commands/metrics.py): verify total_input_tokens, total_output_tokens, total_cache_read_tokens, total_cache_creation_tokens, total_reasoning_tokens, provider_cache_hit_rate (cache_read / total_input), cache_hit_rate (cache_hits / total_requests), tool_calls_pruned (tool_outputs_omitted), tokens_reduced, chars_saved, avg_ttft_ms (sum_ttft_ms / count_ttft), avg_prefill_throughput_tps, latest_prefill_tps, avg_tail_prefill_tps, latest_tail_prefill_tps, avg_decode_throughput_tps and latest_decode_throughput_tps are computed with identical formulas, identical zero/None guards and identical rounding in the live in-memory proxy, the /holon/ dashboard, the terminal scorecard and the offline wire-log parser. 4) TESTS: add comprehensive unit tests in tests/test_mitm_addon.py and tests/test_cli.py asserting exact prefill and decode tok/s for streaming and non-streaming responses, asserting non-streaming requests never enter the decode average, asserting sub-50ms generation windows are rejected, asserting missing-timing samples do not produce 0.00 prefill, and asserting live and offline metric aggregation agree. 5) VERIFICATION: keep uv run task lint and uv run task test fully green.

questions.question: Should decode throughput be reported as 0.00 for non-streaming requests or omitted entirely?
questions.answer: Omitted. Non-streaming decode throughput is physically meaningless, so the per-request value is reported as null/unmeasured and the request never contributes to avg_decode_throughput_tps.

questions.question: What streaming duration floor should reject unreliable decode samples?
questions.answer: 0.05 seconds, matching the acceptance criteria in Bean 0097.

questions.question: May the fix change the JSON contract of /holon/api/metrics?
questions.answer: Only additively. Existing keys keep their names and semantics; unmeasured throughput values become null instead of a fabricated float.

goal: Build an extensive A/B testing suite and operator documentation for evaluating holon-coherence token reduction, cache hit efficacy, and latency metrics: 1) A/B TESTING HARNESS / RUNNER (src/holon_coherence/commands/ab_test.py): Implement 'holon-coherence ab-test' CLI command that takes multi-turn agent payload traces and executes reproducible comparisons between Variant A (Baseline / Control: unoptimized or HOLON_PASSIVE_MONITORING=1) and Variant B (Optimized / Treatment: active token reduction, payload cleaning, cache breakpoint injection, semantic disk caching). Compute differential scorecards: Total Tokens (input, output, cache read), Context Reduction (% prompt tokens reduced, chars saved), Tool Calls Pruned, Latency & TTFT deltas, and Semantic Parity verification. 2) CLI INTEGRATION: Wire 'ab-test' into holon_coherence.cli dispatch with options for baseline port/mode, optimized port/mode, trace payload file path, rounds, and output formats (table, JSON). 3) INTEGRATION & REGRESSION TEST SUITE (tests/test_ab_testing.py): Comprehensive tests covering multi-turn repetitive tool traces, Anthropic and OpenAI cache breakpoint assertions, SSE streaming delivery equivalence, and statistically significant token reduction assertions (>20% on repetitive tool output traces). 4) OPERATOR DOCUMENTATION (docs/ab_testing_guide.md, README.md): Step-by-step operator guide covering local, Docker, and CI benchmarking, configuration flags, scorecard interpretation, and Rule 10 authentic data sampling methodology. 5) VERIFICATION: 100% clean test passes and ruff lint clean.

questions.question: Should ab-test support both offline replay of transaction logs and live dual-proxy comparison?

description: Execute Bean 0130 in holon-coherence: fix proxy readiness race condition during cold start by polling HTTP metrics endpoint instead of host TCP port, and add agent runner startup integration tests.
goal:
1) FIX PROXY READINESS: In src/holon_coherence/commands/start.py, update wait_for_proxy_ready to actively poll http://127.0.0.1:{port}/holon/api/metrics (or /_holon/metrics) with urllib.request instead of only checking is_port_in_use. Ensure it verifies HTTP 200 from mitmproxy, catches URLError/ConnectionRefusedError/OSError, retries until timeout (PROXY_READY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS), and fails fast if the container stops running.
2) UNIT TESTS: Update TestWaitForProxyReady in tests/test_cli.py to verify HTTP polling behaviour: success on HTTP 200, retries on initial connection failure before succeeding, fail-fast when container exits, and timeout handling.

description: Two holon-coherence changes in one execution: (Bean 0129) expose the plain mitmweb request/response inspection dashboard by default from 'holon-coherence start' with host port-conflict fallback and print every exposed endpoint (proxy, Coherence live dashboard, mitmweb inspector with its access token) from 'status', 'metrics' and 'start' output; (Bean 0133) measure the proxy readiness poll deadline with a monotonic clock so a wall-clock step can neither stretch nor short-circuit cold-start readiness.
goal:
1) BEAN 0133 - MONOTONIC READINESS DEADLINE: in src/holon_coherence/commands/start.py, wait_for_proxy_ready() currently computes 'deadline = time.time() + timeout' and loops on 'while time.time() < deadline', while sibling loops in the same module already use time.monotonic(). Convert the deadline computation and the loop bound to time.monotonic() so the timeout is a duration and not a wall-clock instant. Audit every other time.time() use in the package: convert any that measures an elapsed duration or a timeout deadline, and leave genuine epoch timestamps (log lines, wire records, telemetry timestamps) untouched. Add a regression test that drives the readiness poll with an injected fake clock and asserts (a) a backwards wall-clock step cannot extend the poll, (b) a forwards wall-clock step cannot short-circuit it while the endpoint is still refusing connections, and (c) the poll still returns as soon as the metrics endpoint answers HTTP 200. Follow the fake-clock test style already established for the HTTP readiness polling tests.
2) BEAN 0129 - MITMWEB INSPECTION UI BY DEFAULT: in src/holon_coherence/commands/start.py the mitmweb tool is only selected when '--web' is passed ('tool = "mitmweb" if args.web else "mitmdump"'), so a plain 'holon-coherence start' gives no way to inspect live traffic. Make the mitmweb inspector available without extra flags on a normal start, with a host port-conflict fallback for the inspector port (default 8081, overridable) mirroring the fallback behaviour already used for the proxy and dashboard ports, and keep an explicit opt-out switch so a headless start can still run mitmdump only. Preserve the existing token/password handling: resolve and persist the inspector password/token exactly as the '--web' path does today, pass it to mitmweb so the UI is not unauthenticated, and never print or log the token in a way that leaks it into wire logs. Keep the existing secret scrubbing patterns for logged requests and responses in place and verify they still apply to inspector output.
3) BEAN 0129 - ENDPOINT REPORTING: 'holon-coherence start', 'holon-coherence status' and 'holon-coherence metrics' must each print every exposed endpoint with its actually resolved host:port, namely the proxy listen address, the Coherence live dashboard (the custom metrics UI served under /holon/), and the plain mitmweb inspection URL in the exact form 'http://127.0.0.1:<web_port>/?token=<token>' with a label that makes clear this is raw request/response inspection. When the inspector is not running, say so explicitly instead of printing a stale URL. Keep the terminal table formatting conventions already used by 'metrics'.
4) TESTS: extend the unit tests so the new behaviour is covered without needing Docker: default start selects mitmweb and passes the resolved inspector port plus the token, the opt-out path still selects mitmdump, an occupied inspector port falls back to the next free port, the printed start/status/metrics output contains all three endpoints, and the readiness deadline is monotonic. All tests must run with 'uv run pytest' (integration tests stay marked so 'uv run pytest -m "not integration_test"' passes without Docker). Never use synthetic or mock data to report metrics or benchmark numbers.
5) DOCS: update README.md and the relevant docs/ pages to explain how to open the mitmweb inspector to view live request methods, URLs, headers, request bodies, response status codes and bodies, cache status and TLS details, how the token is resolved and where it is printed, how to opt out, and how the endpoints and ports are reported by start/status/metrics.
6) QUALITY GATES: run 'make lint', 'uv run ruff check .' and 'uv run pytest -m "not integration_test"' and make them pass with zero errors. Format any changed markdown with the repository's own configuration only. Use Australian English spelling in all comments, docstrings and log strings. No new runtime dependencies.

questions.question: Should the mitmweb inspector be enabled by default?
questions.answer: Yes, a plain 'holon-coherence start' must expose the mitmweb inspector on its default port with a port-conflict fallback and token authentication, while an explicit opt-out keeps the headless mitmdump-only behaviour.

questions.question: How must the inspector token be treated?
questions.answer: It must be resolved and persisted exactly as today, passed to mitmweb so the UI stays authenticated, and never written to wire logs or any unsanitised output.

questions.question: Which clock must bound the proxy readiness wait?
questions.answer: time.monotonic(), because the timeout is a duration. Wall-clock time.time() stays only for genuine epoch timestamps.

Append-only provenance records (holon-knowledge/ledger/*.jsonl, plans/, executions/, intents/) are history and are neither edited nor checked.
5) HYGIENE TEST: add tests/test_repo_hygiene.py (pytest only, reading 'git ls-files' output) that fails when a tracked file lives under todo/, .subagent/ or .beans/, or when a tracked file outside the provenance records contains a todo/ or .subagent/ path, a '.beans/' path, an absolute path into a harness checkout, or a task id matching 'Bean' followed by four digits. Match the directory names exactly, so that a future '.beads/' directory or file is not rejected, and add a test proving that. The repository's own .agents/AGENTS.md is allowed. Build the forbidden patterns so the test file does not match itself. Update affected tests for the new default path.
6) VERIFY: 'git grep' finds no todo/ default or task id outside the provenance records; 'uv run task test' passes.
7) CONSTRAINTS: Australian English in comments, docstrings, docs and log strings; no new dependencies unless this intent explicitly requires one (it does not); keep functions short and low in branching; tests strictly via 'uv run task test' / 'uv run pytest' from the repository root (never PYTHONPATH, never name any other test runner); 'uv run task lint' must pass and every changed Markdown file must pass 'npx prettier --check' (this repository defines no lint-docs task; the requirement is the same check on the changed files, and adding the task is out of scope because pyproject.toml is not in this change's touch set); keep all paths target-native (never reference harness directories such as .beans/, todo/, .agents/, bean ids or review ids in any target file this change writes); never create auxiliary ledgers and keep the three ledgers under holon-knowledge/ledger/ append-only. TOUCH SET: this change may modify only src/holon_coherence/mitm_addon.py, src/holon_coherence/commands/metrics.py, src/holon_coherence/commands/endpoints.py, src/holon_coherence/commands/start.py, src/holon_coherence/metrics_math.py, docs/audit_report.md, docs/methods/*.md, docs/mitm_telemetry_metrics_plan.md, docs/token_reduction_*.md, tests/test_mitm_addon*.py, tests/test_cli.py, tests/test_ab_testing.py, tests/test_host_local.py, tests/test_hybrid_cache.py, tests/test_makefile.py, .gitignore and one new tests/test_repo_hygiene.py (in particular .github/workflows/, pyproject.toml, uv.lock, README.md, the Makefile and .agents/AGENTS.md are off-limits), plus the flow's own append-only ledger rows and its plans/ and executions/ records; every other file is off-limits because concurrent changes own them, and a step that seems to need another file must be dropped and reported in the execution notes instead.

questions.question: Is this one intent or should it split into sub-intents?
questions.answer: One intent. Removing the leaks and adding the test that keeps them out belong together; splitting would land a hygiene test that fails on arrival, or removals with no guard.

questions.question: Why a pytest file instead of a check in test-hygiene.yml or pyproject.toml?
questions.answer: Both files belong to concurrent changes. A pytest hygiene test runs in the existing unit job with no workflow edit.

questions.question: Must the hygiene test reject a '.beads/' directory?
questions.answer: No. It must match the forbidden directory names exactly, and a test must prove that '.beads/' passes.

questions.question: Are the ledgers, plans and execution records rewritten to drop old task ids?
questions.answer: No. They are append-only provenance and stay as recorded; the hygiene test excludes them.
